episode_summary: Episode 218 of The Bitcoin Podcast (August 2018) opens with a market discussion as Bitcoin trades near 6,146 dollars and Ethereum near 309 dollars. The hosts debate whether the downturn is a short lull or a multi-year crypto winter and whether ETF approval timing matters. Corey then interviews Saifedean Ammous about his book The Bitcoin Standard, covering sound money, store of value, deflation and Bitcoin adoption. The episode closes with the hosts explaining Ethereum testnets versus mainnet.

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host predicted that Bitcoin's inflation rate in 2020 would be lower than the US dollar's.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the inflation rate in 2020 will be lower than the U.S. dollar. It will be.

cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So the last winter was two years. This one's going to be from, this one's going to be four to five years.

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host argued that Bitcoin's price would stabilize or rise as it became more useful, since cycles come from trading rather than utility.
cards.speaker: host

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said Bitcoin would not survive a five-year winter and that such a winter might push people to other currencies.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I wouldn't survive a five-year winner. Bitcoin won't.

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said Bitcoin was not moving fast enough to keep up with demand, despite SegWit's two-megabyte blocks.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i don't think it's moving fast enough to keep up with the demand

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host predicted that Ethereum, given the innovation around it, would eventually pass Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: my opinion it'll it'll pass bitcoin eventually

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said Bitcoin's digital scarcity was real because there were only 21 million bitcoins.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it was real digital scarcity there were only 21 million bitcoins

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host argued that a token needs a community around a useful purpose, since digital scarcity alone is no longer rare.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it has to be a community surrounded by a useful token that isn't just there to hold the purpose of the token

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host explained that a testnet is a copy of Ethereum where tokens have no value, so developers can find bugs before mainnet.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's a bunch of test nets, which is basically a copy of Ethereum where the tokens basically have no value

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said Ethereum's mainnet tokens were trading around 300 dollars.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: onto the main net where the tokens have value currently around $300

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host explained that deployed Ethereum smart contracts are immutable, so developers must plan upgrades carefully.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: those smart contracts are immutable, which means that you can't change those smart contracts

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said larger ICO-era projects were only starting to deploy used products on Ethereum mainnet, and CryptoKitties was one of the first useful ones.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: This year, we're starting to see some of those larger projects from the initial ICO days finally deploying products on the mainnet

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said that with a civic identity smart contract on Ethereum, people could theoretically never have to log in anywhere.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: you could theoretically never have to log in anywhere ever

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said that once an Ethereum application has utility that is scarce, the token's value should go up.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: once there is utility to this and that utility is scarce then the value should

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said an application released on Ethereum mainnet saw its altcoin plummet, which they did not think was connected to the launch.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's a funfair was uh released on mainnet and their altcoin plummeted

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said Bitcoin dominance was back up to 50 percent while the total crypto market cap was about 208 billion dollars.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: BTC dominance is back up to 50%

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host said they had found a vulnerability in a test network application that would have been valuable to exploit on mainnet.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i found a vulnerability in that test net while i was doing there

cards.claim: In August 2018 a host explained that deploying straight to mainnet with real value gives attackers an incentive to steal, so vulnerabilities should be found on testnets first.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if you go straight to main net and there's value, then everyone is incentivized to steal from you as opposed to help you.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said sound money is money chosen and valued by people, while unsound money is imposed by force.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: It's sound money or unsound money.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said sound money trades freely while unsound money trades based on someone's edict.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: So sound money trades freely. Unsound money trades based on somebody's edict.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said that by the end of the 19th century almost everywhere in the world was using gold as money.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: pretty much everywhere in the world by the end of the 19th century, everybody was using gold as money

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous argued Bitcoin qualifies as sound money because nobody forces anyone to accept it and it has a market price.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: nobody forces anybody to accept it as money. It is accepted on its own terms

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said Bitcoin was becoming more like money as more people held it as a store of value.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: Bitcoin is becoming more and more like money.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous predicted Bitcoin would first gain market share as a store of value before it was widely spent.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: Bitcoin is first going to gain market share as a store of value.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous estimated that less than 1 percent of the world owned Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: less than 1% of the world, I would say, owns Bitcoin

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said that while dollars are accepted, people are better off spending dollars and keeping Bitcoin for the future.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: As long as people will accept your dollars, you are better off just giving them the dollars

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous defined a store of value as anything used to hold value for future exchange.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: a store of value is anything that you use in order to store value into the future

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous argued that when Bitcoin rises in value, people spend less, since people are more careful with money that holds its value.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: people are going to be more careful about the money that they spend. if the value of the money declines, people are far more reckless with what they spend.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said progress and civilization start when people delay gratification to save and invest.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: That's what initiates the process of civilization is the ability of people to delay their gratification

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said a crash may be needed for people to see the current system is unsustainable, though a gradual shift to saving is also possible.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: There's always the possibility that we're going to have to get a crash for people to realize this is not sustainable and that it's going to be painful.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous pointed to 36-month 0 percent interest offers on flat-screen TVs in the US as a sign of easy money.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: the fact that you can get 36 months 0% interest on buying a flat screen TV

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said Bitcoin should not be sold as a cool iPhone-style technology, since it is not what people want.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: you know, Bitcoin is not a cool iPhone. It's not what you want.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous described Bitcoin as the medicine people need, not the toy they want, a metaphor for its bitter but beneficial use.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: Bitcoin is the medicine that you need.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous predicted that how Bitcoin works will become as arcane to most people as how a car or refrigerator works.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: the day will come when this will be as uh arcane to most people as the knowledge of how your car works or how your refrigerator works

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous said the Bitcoin supply cannot be controlled by anybody, which is the key point of its design.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: And it's a currency whose supply cannot be controlled by anybody.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous predicted that a Bitcoin economy would give people more freedom and reduce government control because governments would lose the ability to print money.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: I think a Bitcoin economy will see people have more freedom in what they do, and they will have less control for government because government will lose its ability to print money.

cards.claim: In August 2018 Saifedean Ammous argued that business cycles, inflation and unemployment are simply a function of fake, easy money.
cards.speaker: Saifedean Ammous
cards.quote: these are just simply a function of fake, easy money.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #218: Saifedean Ammous
